methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waabi, a Series C autonomous transportation company founded by Raquel Urtasun, is evaluated against a sector universe of seven private transportation companies, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in this frontier segment.

Due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers within transportation (zero same-stage, zero adjacent-stage datapoints meeting clustering thresholds), peer-median valuation was not applicable. The analysis therefore relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to Waabi's $1.0B total capital raised proxy. This approach yields an implied valuation of $1.7B.

The triangulated valuation range of $1.4B to $2.0B (median $1.7B) reflects limited methodological diversity and is anchored primarily to typical Series C advancement multiples rather than market comparables. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable private transactions at similar scale and stage, the nascent nature of autonomous transportation commercial deployment, and the difficulty isolating valuation-relevant metrics (path to unit economics, commercialization timeline) across the peer set. Resolution of these uncertainties would materially refine any range.
